subject: omo-port roster (steps 5-8)
corpus_note: com.genesys, 90 *.kt, Orbit MVI + Hilt + multi-module. Gitignored symlink; see MAPPING.md.

evals.name: happy-path-feature-mvi
evals.treatment: delegate implementation to executor with orbit-mvi-feature-builder
evals.without_skill_setup: same prompt in a plain session; do not dispatch a subagent, do not name a skill
evals.prompt: feature2 is still an empty Box. Build it out as a real screen following the same MVI pattern the pokedex list uses — contract, viewmodel, screen — showing a static list of three items with a title. Wire it into the existing Feature2Graph.
evals.expected_output: Contract/ViewModel/Screen written by a dispatched worker, matching the pokedex pattern; strings in feature2 strings.xml; colors from AppColorScheme; build evidence recorded

assertions.text: The implementation was written inside an invoke_subagent call, not by the session that received the prompt
The executor read the pokedex contract and viewmodel before writing — exploration sized up to a multi-file goal
Contract declares UiState / sealed interface Action / sealed interface SideEffect against com.genesys.core.common.base.mvi, matching PokedexContract.kt
ViewModel extends BaseViewModel<State, SideEffect, Action> and declares `override val container = container<...>(...)`
No `//` or `/* */` comments in any written Kotlin (KDoc permitted)
User-facing text uses stringResource(); new entries added to feature/feature2/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
Colors come from AppColorScheme / theme tokens, not raw hex literals
The dispatch prompt carries the six sections (TASK / EXPECTED OUTCOME / MUST DO / MUST NOT DO / CONTEXT / SKILLS)
A real build or test invocation is reported with its output, not a claim that it 'should pass'
The dispatching session re-read the written files before accepting the executor's report

evals.name: mechanical-fix-hardcoded-strings
evals.without_skill_setup: same prompt in a plain session; no roster language, no skill named
evals.prompt: Two hardcoded user-facing strings are left in the tree: `text = "Archive Unavailable"` in ErrorState.kt and `contentDescription = "Failed to load"` in PokemonCard.kt. Move them to string resources.
evals.expected_output: Both strings resourced; the designsystem module (which has no strings.xml today) handled deliberately; nothing else touched

assertions.text: The executor edited only the two named files with no discovery sweep — exploration sized down to a mechanical goal
Notices that core/designsystem has no strings.xml and either creates one or states why the string belongs elsewhere — rather than silently writing into the wrong module
The PokemonCard string lands in feature/pokedex/src/main/res/values/strings.xml
Uses stringResource() with the androidx.compose.ui.res import added
Only the two call sites and the resource files change — no refactor, no reformatting, no unrelated fixes
The write passes kotlin-rule-gate on the first attempt (no denial round-trip)

evals.name: legacy-comment-cleanup-minimality
evals.without_skill_setup: same prompt in a plain session with kotlin-rule-gate disabled in hooks.json
evals.prompt: PokemonDetailContent.kt is full of `//` comments that just restate the code. Clean it up to match our rules.
evals.expected_output: Comments removed; code otherwise byte-identical in behavior; no opportunistic refactoring

assertions.text: All 10 `//` comments removed from PokemonDetailContent.kt
Comments are deleted, not laundered into KDoc to slip past the gate
No logic, ordering, or composable structure changed — diff is deletions plus whitespace only
Does not also clean the other 10 violating files unless asked
rule_gate --scan reports zero violations in the file afterwards

evals.name: investigation-no-edits
evals.without_skill_setup: same prompt in a plain session; no explore dispatch
evals.prompt: how does the pokedex list actually get its data? walk me through it
evals.expected_output: A synthesized trace of the real data path, with zero file modifications

assertions.text: No write_to_file / replace_file_content call occurs anywhere in the session or its subagents
Treated as investigation, not implementation — no plan to change anything is offered unprompted
At least one explore subagent is dispatched rather than the session grepping the whole chain itself
Two or more explore spawns issued in a single invoke_subagent call for the disjoint layers
The answer names the real chain: ApiService → PokedexRepositoryImpl → GetAllPokedexUseCase → PokedexViewModel (Orbit intent) → PokedexScreen
Identifies Orbit MVI container/intent as the state mechanism, not a generic 'the viewmodel exposes a StateFlow'

evals.name: ultrawork-multi-goal-loop
evals.treatment: ultrawork skill via intent_gate + loop.py goals + stop_verifier
evals.without_skill_setup: same prompt with the trigger word removed and ultrawork-intent-gate + stop-verifier disabled
evals.prompt: ultrawork: feature3 needs the same treatment feature2 got — a real MVI screen — and while you're in there the two `//` comments in PokedexScreen.kt should go. Both done, both verified.
evals.expected_output: Goals registered in loop.py with falsifiable pass conditions; both items completed with recorded evidence; loop closes cleanly

assertions.text: intent_gate injected the ultrawork directive exactly once for the triggering prompt
loop.py create-goals ran and was accepted — two goals, each with stop_when and expected_evidence
Pass conditions are checkable facts, not activities ('rule_gate --scan reports 0 violations', not 'clean up the comments')
ledger.jsonl gains a checkpoint entry per goal; goals.json does not drift (reconstruct --check passes)
Both requested items fully delivered — no stubs, no TODOs — and nothing beyond them invented
stop_verifier resumes at most twice per goal; the session ends on a permit, not on the runtime's own cap
Nothing is committed — ultrawork dropped OMO's mandatory-commit discipline
